To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the co-presence in the organism of two halogenated compounds, such as carbon tetrachioride (CT) and 1,2 dichloroethane(DCE) (DBE), exerts a synergistic effect on liver necroses and on the production of TBA-reactive substance (TRAS) by liver homogenate incubated at 370C.
the co-presence with carbon tetrachloide of 1,2 dichloroethane, which is a solvent for the former and a solvent and an anesthetic for the latter, has an additive effect on liver toxicity.
the co-presence in the body of two halogenated compounds can exert a potentiating effect on liver toxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synergistic effect of two halogen compounds on liver damage, with particular regard to the mechanism of action of this effect.
the effect of the co-presence in the organism of two halogen compounds, both of which are hepatotoxic.
the effects of halogenated hydrocarbons on lipid peroxidation, which is a key event in the pathogenesis of liver injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the co-presence in the organism of two halogen compounds, each of which is toxic for the liver, can lead to a potentiation of liver injury.
halogen compounds can exert synergistic actions in the liver damage, but the mechanism of this phenomenon is still unknown.

the synergistic action of the halogenated hydrocarbons is not related to the presence of a specific chemical structure but is rather related to the presence in the molecule of an electronegative atom (Cl, Br, F) that is able to form a complex with GSH and to be involved in a reaction with O2- to form a radical species that is able to react with GSH and/or with the cell membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the co-presence in the body of halogenated compounds, which are metabolised by the same enzymes, exerts a poteniating effect in vivo on liver toxicity.
the synergistic action of the mixture is due to a mechanism involving the inhibition of lipid peroxidation.
the synergism between the two halogen compounds depends on the type of interaction between the two molecules and not on their chemical nature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the co-presence, in the same animal, of two hepatotoxins that are not directly related to each other can produce an effect on the target organ that is more severe than that produced by each of them.
the co-presence with DCE of CT, DBE or other halogenated alkanes, exerts a synergistic effect on liver toxicity.
, when a mixture of two hepatotoxic halogenated aliphatic compounds is administered, the toxicity of the mixture is not equal to the sum of the toxicities of the two compounds.
